PullRequest.Title: Add integrator id to headers for aligned experimentation
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Adds `integratorid: vscode-chat` to experiment request headers and new-API targeting parameters in VS Code core and Copilot Chat. This aligns client targeting with CAPI when an experiment selects **Integrator = VS Code**.

Scenarios.Scenario: VS Code core experiment-service initialization and hourly/filter-triggered assignment refresh
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The delayed WorkbenchAssignmentService is created on first use, loads tas-client, constructs the existing client, and performs its existing legacy and optional assignments fetches. Treatment reads await client setup and use the existing memento/cache behavior while initial network initialization is pending. The diff only adds a constant filter/header and a shallow header copy; it adds no await or boundary to this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dynamically load the tas-client module during service setup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per TAS client generation; generations occur on initial delayed construction and existing account endpoint changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same module load occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before constructing the client, but is unchanged and the added metadata does not affect module loading.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch legacy TAS assignments using the existing tas-client endpoint and filter provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing legacy endpoint operation per library-defined initial fetch/refetch, subject to the unchanged one-hour cadence and filter-change refreshes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same legacy request occurred with one fewer filter/header value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of the existing assignment initialization/refresh; the diff adds one small targeting filter but no request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST to the account-provided /api/v1/assignments endpoint through IRequestService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing assignments operation per library-defined initial fetch/refetch when an account endpoint exists; no per-treatment fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same POST, body, request service, and cadence were used without integratorid.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of existing initialization/refresh and can affect treatment freshness; the diff only copies the existing small header object and appends one constant header.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist TAS state through the existing application memento.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing writes when tas-client updates assignment state; unchanged by the added fixed metadata field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same memento was read and saved under the same storage key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Storage behavior is unchanged and no new write is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One fixed metadata field per filter set/request, independent of treatment count, extension count, or workspace size. Client generations scale only with pre-existing account endpoint changes; refreshes remain on the existing one-hour timer or existing filter-change events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Scheduling remains owned by tas-client. The existing legacy and assignments requests may run according to the library's unchanged initialization/refresh policy; the diff adds no loop, Promise fan-out, queue, or additional concurrent operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing application-scoped memento remains the warm cache, with the same storage key and writes. The assignments request was already made with disableCache=true, and the one-hour refetch interval is unchanged. No cache key, invalidation, negative-cache, or coalescing behavior changes client-side.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: changed lines add only one Map entry and one shallow spread per existing request, while traced setup, polling, storage, and request call sites retain identical cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact TAS endpoint latency and whether the library schedules its two existing endpoints concurrently are library/runtime dependent, but the diff does not alter endpoint count or scheduling. The added object/map entry and bytes are constant and negligible relative to the existing request.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change adds constant-size serialization/allocation to an already infrequent network path without adding boundary calls, fan-out, retention, or critical-path blocking.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot Chat experimentation delegate creation, token-endpoint replacement, and periodic refresh
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Extension activation creates the experimentation delegate and its existing initial fetch; hasTreatments and explicit refreshes await existing TAS work. Token endpoint changes can replace the delegate, and the existing hourly timer refreshes it. The diff adds the integrator to provider output and clones/appends one header immediately before the same fetch call, with no extra asynchronous step.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Require product.json to read the release date when constructing CopilotAssignmentsFilterProvider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per assignments filter-provider/delegate generation when the assignments endpoint exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same product.json read occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs during existing delegate construction; the diff does not add or repeat this read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Issue the existing legacy TAS GET through FetcherService and its configured fallback transports.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical legacy request per existing initial/refresh cycle; failure-only transport fallback remains unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same GET and fallback policy ran without integratorid.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing assignment initialization/refresh boundary; the diff only shallow-copies a small header object and appends one constant header.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Issue the existing assignments POST through FetcherService when the Copilot token provides an exp endpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical POST per existing initial/refresh cycle when enabled, with unchanged failure-only transport fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same POST, body, endpoint, and fetch transport ran without integratorid.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing assignment initialization/refresh boundary; no new request or wait is introduced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist assignment state and user information through the existing extension globalState memento.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing writes on user-info or assignment-state changes; adding a request/filter field does not create a new persistence event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same globalState keys and assignment storage were used.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Persistence ownership and revocation remain unchanged; no diff-added write is present.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One fixed filter/header field per logical legacy GET or assignments POST. Frequency is bounded by existing initial delegate creation, endpoint changes, user-info/completions refresh events, and the one-hour timer, not by chat messages or treatment reads.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing delegate generation/revocation and tas-client scheduling are unchanged. FetcherService fallback may serially try configured transports on failures, but the same options object carries the added header and the diff does not increase fallback count or create a burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing VS Code globalState remains the warm assignment cache, and delegate replacement/revocation is unchanged. Fetcher cache mode selection and TAS refresh behavior are unchanged; the diff adds metadata but no new cache, cache miss retry, or invalidation path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the adapter, timer, delegate lifecycle, token replacement path, and fetch fallback were traced, and all changed work is constant-size local metadata preparation on existing calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual network latency and failure fallback prevalence vary by proxy and transport, but endpoint cardinality and fallback scheduling are unchanged. The fixed extra header/map entry cannot scale with chat activity or assignment count.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. There is no added network operation, retry, concurrency, eager I/O, or retained state; only constant-size metadata is attached to existing requests.

Scenarios.Scenario: Experiment filter materialization for legacy and assignments APIs in core and Copilot Chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Filter providers are queried by the existing TAS clients while preparing existing assignment requests. The changed enum cases and Map.set add one constant key/value during that preparation; standalone treatment reads consume cached client state and do not newly invoke this work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize/filter existing TAS request metadata, now including integratorid.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional constant string pair per existing filter materialization and downstream request; effective cardinality is fixed at one after provider merging.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing providers built and serialized the same bounded filter maps without this one field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds constant bytes and one Map insertion before an existing request, without adding an extra serialization pass.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize Copilot assignments parameters, now including integratorid.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional constant string pair per existing assignments filter materialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same bounded map was serialized without integratorid.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Constant synchronous work before an existing request; it does not scale with account organization list beyond the pre-existing fields.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly one additional entry per produced filter map. Cost does not grow with number of treatments, workspace resources, UI rows, or request history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Filter construction is synchronous within each existing request preparation. No background task, listener, limiter, or concurrent operation is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Providers already construct fresh small maps per TAS request. The diff neither defeats a cached filter result nor changes assignment-state caching/coalescing; it increases each map by one entry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete changed hunks and provider loops: only one enum value/Map insertion is added to bounded maps.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact library serialization implementation is external, but the effective added input is demonstrably one short constant key/value, so there is no realistic scaling mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The introduced CPU, allocation, and wire-size cost is fixed and too small to create latency, throughput, memory, or GC degradation.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and traced core and Copilot experimentation initialization, refresh, cache, storage, and network paths. The PR preserves request count, cadence, concurrency, caching, and lifecycle; it adds only one bounded metadata field and small per-request object/map work, so no performance finding was submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
